about: B-34 (v19.5, 7 Nov 2026). One place for blood-test timing, aims and when to talk to the prescriber. build.py draws the tables on /monitoring (sections with "levels": group id), the 'Blood tests' box on each medicine page, and the blood-test record printable reads the rows marked printable. 'aim' and 'talkIf' are patient wording; 'clinician' is one line under 'For clinicians'; 'other' shows as 'Other guidance'. Sources are cited by id; build.py turns them into each page's reference numbers (an existing reference with the same URL, and the 'match' words if given, is reused; otherwise the source's own text is added). Research: claude/monitoring-research-2026-11-07.md. v19.5 R2 (7 Nov 2026): 'sheets' = one /monitoring section, one printable (file) and the box on its medicine 'pages' per medicine and route; a /monitoring section names its sheet with "levels": sheet id; 'key' is the printable's Key points line.

AUS26.name: AusPATH 2026
AUS26.text: AusPATH (Australian Professional Association for Trans Health). Australian Standards of Care for Informed Consent Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy, version 2 (2026; the document's footer reads "AusPATH SOC 2025"). First published 1 December 2025; this PDF is dated 30 April 2026. Accessed 7 November 2026.

MJA19.name: 2019 position statement
MJA19.text: Cheung AS, Wynne K, Erasmus J, Murray S, Zajac JD. Position statement on the hormonal management of adult transgender and gender diverse individuals. Med J Aust. 2019;211(3):127-33. Accessed 7 November 2026.

EQX20.name: Equinox guide 2020
EQX20.text: Cundill P, Wong P, Cheung A. Hormone therapy prescribing guide for general practitioners working with trans, gender diverse and non-binary patients, version 3.0. Equinox Gender Diverse Health Centre, Thorne Harbour Health; July 2020. Accessed 7 November 2026.

ES17.name: Endocrine Society 2017
ES17.text: Hembree WC, Cohen-Kettenis PT, Gooren L, et al. Endocrine treatment of gender-dysphoric/gender-incongruent persons: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2017;102(11):3869-903 (Tables 14 and 15). Accessed 7 November 2026.

SOC8.name: WPATH SOC8
SOC8.text: Coleman E, Radix AE, Bouman WP, et al. Standards of Care for the Health of Transgender and Gender Diverse People, Version 8. Int J Transgend Health. 2022;23(Suppl 1):S1-259. Accessed 7 November 2026.

RCH23.name: RCH standards 2023
RCH23.text: Telfer MM, Tollit MA, Pace CC, Pang KC. Australian Standards of Care and Treatment Guidelines for Trans and Gender Diverse Children and Adolescents, version 1.4 (appendices 1 and 2: monitoring on puberty blockers and on gender-affirming hormones). Melbourne: The Royal Children's Hospital; 2023. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-REA.name: Reandron 1000 PI
PI-REA.text: Reandron 1000 (testosterone undecanoate) injection, Australian Product Information, sections 4.2 Dose and method of administration and 4.4 Special warnings and precautions (haemoglobin and haematocrit checked periodically) (date of revision 11 December 2025). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-TGL.name: Testogel PI
PI-TGL.text: Testogel (testosterone 1%) gel, Australian Product Information, sections 4.2 Dose and method of administration (testosterone measured in the morning before application) and 4.4 Special warnings and precautions (date of revision 7 October 2025). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-TVN.name: Testavan PI
PI-TVN.text: Testavan (testosterone 2% w/w) gel, Australian Product Information, section 4.2 Dose and method of administration (testosterone measured 2 to 4 hours after application, about 14 and 35 days after starting or a dose change) (date of revision 22 April 2026). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-AF5.name: AndroForte 5 PI
PI-AF5.text: AndroForte 5 (testosterone 5%) transdermal cream, Australian Product Information, section 4.2 Dose and method of administration (monitoring: trough testosterone) (date of revision 10 August 2023). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-PRI.name: Primoteston Depot and Sustanon 250 PI
PI-PRI.text: Primoteston Depot (testosterone enantate; date of revision 13 January 2026) section 4.2 Dose and method of administration and 4.4 Special warnings and precautions, and Sustanon 250 (testosterone esters; 23 February 2026) section 4.4, Australian Product Information (testosterone measured before and during treatment; haemoglobin and haematocrit checked periodically). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-CPA.name: Androcur PI
PI-CPA.text: Androcur (cyproterone acetate) tablets, Australian Product Information, sections 4.3 Contraindications (meningioma) and 4.4 Special warnings and precautions (liver function, adrenocortical function and red cells; liver deaths at 100 mg a day and above; meningioma with long-term use at 25 mg a day and above) (date of revision 25 November 2024). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-SPI.name: Spiractin CMI and Aldactone PI
PI-SPI.text: Spiractin (spironolactone) tablets, Australian Consumer Medicine Information (blood tests: weekly at the start, monthly for 3 months, every 3 months for a year, then every 6 months) (July 2025); Aldactone Product Information sections 4.3 and 4.4 (hyperkalaemia) (date of revision 18 June 2025). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-BIC.name: Cosudex PI
PI-BIC.text: AstraZeneca Pty Ltd. Cosudex (bicalutamide) Australian Product Information, section 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use (liver; QT interval; interstitial lung disease; glucose tolerance with LHRH agonists) and section 4.5 Interactions (warfarin). Date of revision 9 July 2026. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-ZOL.name: Zoladex PI
PI-ZOL.text: Zoladex 3.6 mg implant (goserelin), Australian Product Information, sections 4.4 and 4.5, QT/QTc interval prolongation (date of revision 6 March 2026); the same QT warning is in the Eligard, Lucrin Depot and Diphereline PIs. Therapeutic Goods Administration. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-E2.name: Oestradiol PI
PI-E2.text: Estradot (estradiol) transdermal patch, Australian Product Information, section 4.4 Special warnings and precautions (high triglycerides; liver impairment) (date of revision 8 July 2024). Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

PI-PRO.name: Prometrium PI
PI-PRO.text: Prometrium (progesterone) capsules, Australian Product Information, sections 4.4 and 4.5. Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

FIN.name: Finasteride PI
FIN.text: Finasteride GH 1 (finasteride 1 mg) tablets, Australian Consumer Medicine Information and Product Information (PSA lowered by about 50%). ACSQHC Medicine Finder. Accessed 7 November 2026.

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review. Take the sample just before your next tablet (the lowest point). Splitting the dose or letting tablets dissolve under the tongue changes the result. Rechecked 6 to 8 weeks after a dose change.
rows.aim: Above about 250 pmol/L, with no fixed upper limit
rows.talkIf: It is below about 250 pmol/L, or much higher than expected: the timing of the test is checked first
rows.clinician: Trough target; high results: check timing, contamination and biotin, ask about side effects and weigh risk factors before a gradual, shared dose reduction. Bone loss likely below about 180 pmol/L. ES17/SOC8: 367 to 734 pmol/L (100 to 200 pg/mL).
rows.short: Oestradiol, tablets: just before the next tablet; above about 250 pmol/L

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review. Take the sample just before you put on a new patch. Rechecked 6 to 8 weeks after a dose change.
rows.aim: Above about 250 pmol/L, with no fixed upper limit
rows.talkIf: It is below about 250 pmol/L, or much higher than expected: the timing of the test is checked first
rows.clinician: AusPATH: limited guidance for patches; consider testing before a new patch is applied (level peaks after a new patch).
rows.short: Oestradiol, patches: just before a new patch; above about 250 pmol/L

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review, after at least 3 to 5 days on the same dose. Take the sample before that day's gel, from the arm you did not put gel on. Rechecked 6 to 8 weeks after a dose change.
rows.aim: Above about 250 pmol/L, with no fixed upper limit
rows.talkIf: It is much higher than expected: gel left on the skin where the blood was taken can make the result look far too high
rows.clinician: Trough; steady state 3 to 5 days; venipuncture from the non-application arm (contamination from topical oestrogen at the collection site gives falsely high results); split dosing changes the level.
rows.short: Oestradiol, gel: before the day's gel, from the other arm; above about 250 pmol/L

rows.when: Usually every 3 months for the first year after the first implant, then less often. Implants are not used to start therapy.
rows.aim: Above about 250 pmol/L; the level guides when the next implant is due
rows.talkIf: The level is falling towards 250 pmol/L: ask when the next implant is due
rows.clinician: No data to guide testing; levels above 600 to 734 pmol/L are more likely with implants and injections. Modelled fall to about 250 pmol/L about 4 months after a first 100 mg implant and 13 months after later ones.
rows.short: Oestradiol, implants: about every 3 months in the first year; above about 250 pmol/L

rows.when: At each review, midway between injections, or as a pair of tests (just after and just before an injection) if your prescriber asks. Oestradiol injections are rarely used in Australia.
rows.aim: Above about 250 pmol/L
rows.talkIf: It is much higher or lower than expected
rows.clinician: No data to guide testing; consider peak and trough, or mid-interval. Clot risk similar to oral oestradiol.

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review (every 3 to 4 months in the first year, then about once a year)
rows.aim: Below 2 nmol/L, if you want full suppression
rows.talkIf: It stays above 2 nmol/L when you want full suppression: the blocker or the dose is usually reviewed
rows.clinician: On spironolactone, testosterone may not fall below 2 nmol/L; judge its effect clinically. For bone protection keep endogenous testosterone above 7 nmol/L or oestradiol above 180 pmol/L (LH suppression shows adequacy, but not on cyproterone). ES17/SOC8: below 1.7 nmol/L (50 ng/dL).
rows.short: Testosterone (on oestradiol): at each review; below 2 nmol/L if full suppression is wanted

rows.test: Full blood count, kidney function and electrolytes, liver function
rows.when: Before starting, then at each review
rows.aim: Within the range that fits your body on hormones (see Reading your results)
rows.talkIf: Your prescriber flags a result. Kidney checks matter more if you take spironolactone or PrEP
rows.clinician: Use affirmed-gender ranges for Hb/Hct (haematocrit aligns after about 6 months on oestradiol); eGFR uses the recorded sex, so read the trend. Liver: oestradiol is poorly metabolised in liver impairment.

rows.when: Before starting. After that, not routine
rows.aim: No fixed aim. LH may be checked to see whether your hormone levels are high enough to protect your bones (this does not work on cyproterone)
rows.clinician: LH suppression indicates adequate sex-steroid exposure for bone, except on cyproterone.

rows.when: Before starting. After that, only if your prescriber chooses to check it, or if you have symptoms. Best taken in the morning, about 3 to 4 hours after waking, with no hard exercise beforehand
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: You have new headaches, changes in your vision, or a lot of milky nipple discharge
rows.clinician: No clear evidence for routine monitoring; strongly recommended with galactorrhoea, new headaches, visual disturbance or pituitary hormone deficiency; rises mainly with cyproterone. Other guidance: ES17 suggests periodic prolactin monitoring on oestrogen.

rows.when: Before starting, especially with heart risk factors; then periodically. Ask whether you need to fast: most hormone tests do not need it
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: Your prescriber flags a change
rows.clinician: Pre-existing high triglycerides can rise further on oestrogen, with a risk of pancreatitis. MJA19 lists fasting lipids and glucose at baseline; AusPATH lists fasting glucose with risk factors.

rows.when: Not a routine hormone test. Hormones and genital surgery leave the prostate in place
rows.aim: Read knowing that hormones lower PSA (and finasteride roughly halves it)
rows.talkIf: Anyone orders a PSA test: tell them you take hormones, and finasteride if you do
rows.clinician: GAHT lowers PSA to levels like androgen deprivation; risk is lower but remains; no consensus PSA thresholds.

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review. The product leaflet suggests more often at first: weekly, then monthly for 3 months, then every 3 months for a year, then every 6 months
rows.aim: Within the lab's range

other.text: potassium every 3 months in the first year, then yearly

rows.talkIf: Potassium is flagged high, your kidney result drops, or you start a blood-pressure tablet (ACE inhibitor or ARB), an anti-inflammatory (NSAID), a potassium supplement or a salt substitute
rows.clinician: Hyperkalaemia contraindicates spironolactone. eGFR uses the recorded sex; read the trend. Upper GI bleeding signal, especially at 100 mg and age 55 to 75.

sources.loc: p27, p28, p36, Table 8 p37, p53

rows.when: At each review, as in the oestradiol table
rows.aim: Spironolactone may not bring testosterone below 2 nmol/L; its effect is judged by your body changes
rows.talkIf: The changes are not what you hoped for
rows.clinician: Efficacy should be assessed clinically, not by serum testosterone alone.

rows.when: At each review
rows.aim: Not too low for you
rows.talkIf: You feel dizzy or light-headed, especially when you stand up
rows.clinician: Monitor electrolytes/eGFR and low BP.

rows.when: Before starting, regularly during treatment, and at once if you have signs of liver trouble
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: You have yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine: get checked straight away
rows.clinician: Fatal hepatotoxicity reported at 100 mg a day and above (dose related); stop if liver injury is confirmed. Australian feminising doses: 12.5 mg once a week up to 25 mg a day.

rows.when: No routine scan. Your prescriber keeps your dose, and your total dose over the years, as low as works
rows.aim: The lowest dose that works
rows.talkIf: You have new or worsening headaches, changes in your vision, a seizure, or new weakness: tell your prescriber promptly
rows.clinician: Meningioma with long-term use at 25 mg a day and above (PI s4.4; contraindicated with present or past meningioma, s4.3); AusPATH: association with more than 50 mg a day or more than 10 g cumulative, monitor cumulative lifetime dose. The PI threshold equals the top of the AusPATH dose range.

rows.when: At each review; this is how cyproterone's effect is checked
rows.aim: Below 2 nmol/L, if you want full suppression
rows.talkIf: It stays above 2 nmol/L when you want full suppression
rows.clinician: LH is not a valid check of bone adequacy on cyproterone.

rows.test: Full blood count, adrenal function and prolactin
rows.when: Full blood count before starting and regularly; adrenal function as the product information advises; prolactin if you have symptoms
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: You have new headaches, vision changes or milky nipple discharge (prolactin), or low mood
rows.clinician: PI: monitor liver, adrenocortical function and red cell count. Prolactin rises mainly with cyproterone. Depression reported.

rows.when: Before starting, and regularly during treatment. It matters most in the first 6 months, when most liver changes happen
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: You have yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine: get checked straight away
rows.clinician: PI: consider periodic LFTs, most changes within the first 6 months; stop if jaundice. AusPATH: not first-line; regular LFTs throughout. Serum testosterone does not reflect its effect (median 7.7 nmol/L on 25 to 50 mg in a case series).

rows.when: ECG and electrolytes if you have a heart rhythm condition or take medicines that affect heart rhythm. INR checks if you take warfarin
rows.talkIf: You take warfarin, or start a medicine that affects heart rhythm
rows.clinician: QT prolongation: consider periodic ECG and electrolytes. Warfarin effect increased; monitor INR. Reduced glucose tolerance reported with LHRH agonists.

rows.when: No routine test
rows.talkIf: You have a new cough, breathlessness or fever: tell your prescriber at once
rows.clinician: Interstitial lung disease, including fatal cases, added to PI s4.4 (rev 9 July 2026; TGA safety update August 2026).

rows.test: Review (no blood test specific to progesterone)
rows.when: A check after 3 to 6 months to see whether it is helping and whether to continue; then at each review with your oestradiol tests
rows.aim: No blood level to aim for
rows.talkIf: You have low mood, or it is not doing what you hoped
rows.clinician: Clinical review after 3 to 6 months to assess effectiveness. PI: caution with depression, epilepsy, migraine, asthma, diabetes, hypertension, fluid retention; may raise ciclosporin levels.

rows.test: Testosterone level (long-acting injection: Reandron and other undecanoate brands)
rows.when: Just before the next injection is due. Not tested or changed until after the first 3 injections; after a dose or interval change, usually 2 more injections before the next test
rows.aim: About 10 to 20 nmol/L just before the injection
rows.talkIf: It is below about 10 nmol/L or above about 20 nmol/L just before the injection: the interval or dose may change
rows.clinician: Trough target. Interval usually 10 to 14 weeks (range 7 to more than 20 weeks). ES17: if trough below 13.9 nmol/L (400 ng/dL), shorten the interval.
rows.short: Testosterone, long-acting injection: just before the next injection; about 10 to 20 nmol/L

rows.test: Testosterone level (short-acting injection: enantate or mixed esters)
rows.when: Midway between injections, or as a pair of tests (peak and trough) if your prescriber asks
rows.aim: Within the male reference range on the lab report. The 10 to 20 nmol/L trough figure does not apply to a midway sample

other.text: midway, about 14 to 24 nmol/L (400 to 700 ng/dL)

rows.talkIf: It is outside the male reference range
rows.clinician: Mid-interval or peak and trough, kept within cisgender male reference ranges. Equinox (2020) differs: morning before the injection (trough) for Primoteston. Short-acting IM testosterone carries the highest polycythaemia risk.
rows.short: Testosterone, short-acting injection: midway between injections; within the male range

rows.when: In the morning, before that day's gel, after at least a week on the same dose
rows.aim: About 10 to 20 nmol/L before the day's gel
rows.talkIf: It is below about 10 nmol/L or above about 20 nmol/L
rows.clinician: Trough, morning before application from the 3rd day on (one week seems reasonable). Contamination from the application site is possible: a reasonable precaution (clinical practice, not stated in the sources) is to collect from skin the gel has not touched.
rows.short: Testosterone, Testogel: morning, before the day's gel; about 10 to 20 nmol/L

rows.when: 2 to 4 hours after putting the gel on. About 2 and 5 weeks after starting or a dose change, then at each review
rows.aim: 17.3 to 36.4 nmol/L at that time (for a full dose). The 10 to 20 nmol/L trough figure does not apply
rows.talkIf: It is below 17.3 nmol/L or above 36.4 nmol/L: your prescriber may change the dose by one pump
rows.clinician: PI and AusPATH Table 7 titration bands, measured near peak (about 14 and 35 days after a start or change). ES17/SOC8: transdermal no sooner than 1 week of use, at least 2 hours after application.
rows.short: Testosterone, Testavan: 2 to 4 hours after the gel; 17.3 to 36.4 nmol/L

rows.when: In the morning, before that day's cream, after at least 15 days on the same dose
rows.aim: About 10 to 20 nmol/L before the day's cream
rows.talkIf: It is below about 10 nmol/L or above about 20 nmol/L
rows.clinician: Trough before the day's dose. PI: trough within the lower part of the reference interval for eugonadal men.
rows.short: Testosterone, cream: morning, before the day's cream; about 10 to 20 nmol/L

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review. Checked more closely if you take an SGLT-2 inhibitor (such as empagliflozin or dapagliflozin)
rows.aim: Haematocrit below 0.50 L/L (50%), read against the male range
rows.talkIf: It is 0.50 L/L (50%) or more: smoking, sleep apnoea and lung or kidney problems are checked, and the interval or dose may be changed, or a gel or cream used instead
rows.clinician: Use cisgender male reference ranges for Hb/Hct on testosterone (Hct aligns after about 3 months). Venesection: AusPATH reserves it for primary polycythaemia, with no evidence for use in TGD people (differs from Equinox 2020, which suggests haematology referral for venesection if persistent).
rows.short: Haematocrit on testosterone: at each review; below 0.50 L/L (50%)

rows.when: Before starting, then at each review or as your prescriber decides
rows.aim: Within the lab's range
rows.talkIf: Your prescriber flags a change
rows.clinician: Testosterone lowers HDL and raises triglycerides and LDL. If bone health is a concern, keep testosterone above 7 nmol/L.

rows.when: Before starting, if a pregnancy is possible. Testosterone is not contraception
rows.talkIf: You could be pregnant: testosterone can harm a developing baby, so tell your prescriber straight away
rows.clinician: hCG at baseline if indicated; testosterone is teratogenic.

rows.test: Bone density scan and bone age (young people)
rows.when: Before starting, then as the specialist team decides during treatment
rows.aim: To track bone strength while puberty is paused
rows.talkIf: A scan is overdue, or you have questions about your bones
rows.clinician: RCH: baseline BMD and bone age; BMD at commencement and regular monitoring during treatment recommended; every 12 months as required.

rows.test: Hormone levels: LH, FSH, and oestradiol or testosterone (young people)
rows.when: Before starting; at 6 months, just before the third dose of goserelin or leuprorelin, to check puberty is paused; then every 12 months
rows.aim: LH and FSH low, showing the blocker is working
rows.talkIf: You notice signs of puberty restarting, or a dose was late
rows.clinician: RCH App 1: 6-month LH, FSH and sex steroid just prior to the third dose; yearly FBE, UEC, LFT, lipids, BSL, LH/FSH and sex steroid. Height, weight, BMI and BP every 3 months.

rows.when: Not routine. Considered with risk factors, including long-term use, or a blocker taken without oestrogen or testosterone
rows.talkIf: You have been on a blocker for a long time without oestrogen or testosterone
rows.clinician: DXA does not need to be performed routinely but may be considered with risk factors (prolonged GnRHa, blocker without oestrogen, inadequate oestrogen).

rows.when: If you have a heart rhythm condition or heart failure, or take medicines that affect heart rhythm; then considered periodically
rows.talkIf: You start a medicine that affects heart rhythm
rows.clinician: QT prolongation: correct electrolytes; consider periodic ECG and electrolytes.

sheets.key: Take the blood sample just before your next tablet. Aim: oestradiol above about 250 pmol/L. Testosterone below 2 nmol/L if you want full suppression.
Take the blood sample just before you put on a new patch. Aim: oestradiol above about 250 pmol/L. Testosterone below 2 nmol/L if you want full suppression.
Take the blood sample before that day's gel, from the arm you did not put gel on. Aim: oestradiol above about 250 pmol/L.
Oestradiol is usually checked every 3 months in the first year. The level guides when the next implant is due. Aim: above about 250 pmol/L.
Rarely used in Australia. Oestradiol is checked midway between injections, or before and after one. Aim: above about 250 pmol/L.
Potassium and kidney tests, more often at first. Your oestradiol tests carry on as usual.
Liver tests before and during treatment. Tell your prescriber about new headaches or changes in your vision.
Liver tests, most of all in the first 6 months. A new cough or breathlessness needs checking at once.
No blood test for progesterone itself. A review after 3 to 6 months to see whether it is helping.
Take the blood sample just before the next injection is due. Aim: about 10 to 20 nmol/L. Haematocrit below 0.50 L/L (50%).
Take the blood sample midway between injections. Aim: within the male range on the lab report. Haematocrit below 0.50 L/L (50%).
Testogel: in the morning before that day's gel, about 10 to 20 nmol/L. Testavan: 2 to 4 hours after the gel, 17.3 to 36.4 nmol/L.
Take the blood sample in the morning before that day's cream. Aim: about 10 to 20 nmol/L. Haematocrit below 0.50 L/L (50%).
Young people: a bone scan before starting and hormone checks at 6 months. Adults: a bone scan only with risk factors.

reading._about: v19.5 R3 (Ted, 7 Nov 2026): each sheet's 'reading' names the points from the general 'Reading your results' section of content/monitoring.json that apply to it; levels.py copies the exact wording (matched by these opening words) into the medicine's /monitoring section and its blood test guide PDF. 'units' uses the first sentence only.
reading.timing: A sample taken at a different time
